dedupe_keys.name: altrios advanced locomotive technology and rail infrastructure optimization system

description: ALTRIOS (Advanced Locomotive Technology and Rail Infrastructure Optimization System) is an open-source, fully integrated simulation tool for evaluating strategies to deploy advanced locomotive technologies, including on-board energy storage, and the infrastructure they need. It simulates freight-demand driven train scheduling, mainline meet-pass planning, locomotive and train dynamics, energy conversion efficiencies and energy storage dynamics of line-haul train operations, and its simulation manager runs multi-week operations of a rail network. It was developed by the National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL), the University of Texas at Austin, Southwest Research Institute and BNSF Railway. The core is written in Rust with a Python interface; it installs with pip from PyPI (version 1.1.0, August 2026, Python 3.10 or 3.11) and ships demo scripts and documentation. It is released under a BSD 3-clause licence and is free. It is generic and can be applied to any freight rail network given its track, train and demand data. Caveats: it models line-haul freight operations, not passenger service or detailed signalling, and results depend on the network and powertrain data supplied. It supports capacity planning and optimisation of charging or refuelling infrastructure and locomotive fleets, and network flow studies of freight rail energy use. Related records are the OpenTrack railway simulator and the North American Rail Network.
